gloss: palanquin; sedan chair; a covered litter carried on poles by bearers

definitions.gloss: palanquin; sedan chair; a covered litter carried on poles by bearers
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese conveyance consisting of a cabin mounted on horizontal poles, carried by two or more bearers. Used primarily during the Edo period for transporting nobility and wealthy individuals.

examples.japanese: {殿様|とのさま}が{駕籠|かご}に{乗|の}って{城|しろ}を{出|で}た。
examples.english: The lord left the castle riding in a palanquin.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}には{駕籠|かご}が{主|おも}な{交通手段|こうつうしゅだん}の{一|ひと}つだった。
examples.english: During the Edo period, palanquins were one of the main means of transportation.

examples.japanese: {時代劇|じだいげき}では、{武家|ぶけ}の{女性|じょせい}が{駕籠|かご}に{乗|の}って{嫁入|よめい}りする{場面|ばめん}がよく{描|えが}かれる。
examples.english: In period dramas, scenes of samurai women riding in palanquins for their wedding procession are often depicted.

notes:
A traditional Japanese means of transportation in which a person sits inside a cabin mounted on poles, carried by two or more bearers ({駕籠|かご}{掻|か}き). Used primarily during the Edo period by the nobility, samurai class, and wealthy merchants. Different from {籠|かご} (basket/cage), which shares the same reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {駕籠|かご}に{乗|の}る: to ride in a palanquin
- {駕籠|かご}を{担|かつ}ぐ: to carry a palanquin
- {駕籠|かご}{掻|か}き: palanquin bearer
- お{駕籠|かご}: palanquin (polite)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {籠|かご}: basket, cage — same reading, different meaning
- {御輿|みこし}: portable shrine — carried on poles, but for religious festivals
- {人力車|じんりきしゃ}: rickshaw — later form of human-powered transport
